method: Social vulnerability is the CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index 2022 overall percentile (RPL_THEMES, tracts; missing values coded −999 are left out). The share of residents who are people of colour is SVI E_MINRTY / E_TOTPOP. Poverty is ACS 2020–2024 block-group population below the poverty line over total population, and income is block-group median household income, where a lower income ranks higher. Each is averaged over the tracts or block groups in each res-8 cell and then weighted by GHS-POP 2020 population, so the value describes the people in the radius rather than its land. Residents within the radius is the GHS-POP 2020 total; more people ranks higher, as more people are exposed. The redlined share is the share of the radius in HOLC grade D areas (Mapping Inequality); it covers only cities surveyed in the 1930s, so it has weight 0 in the leaderboard. Scores are mid-rank percentiles (0–100) among the facilities in view, with direction applied so a higher percentile means a greater potential impact; tied values share the midpoint of their rank range, and a facility with no value for a variable is left out of that variable's ranking. The pillar score is the plain mean of the variable percentiles. Neighbourhood variables use the H3 res-8 cells (about 0.7 km² each) whose centre lies within the chosen radius of the facility; site variables use the single res-8 cell that holds the facility point. All of this is provisional.
